name: Example: Finding a Basis for a Given Null Space
problem: Given that  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/412e5084f88d0eb270b0e8a1f5613f85e1cec2c9f89879ccda30ff4c0794fb3d.png) find a basis for $\textrm{Null}(A).$
worked_solution:
Any vector in $\textrm{Null}(A)$ has the form

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/7bba2b6227c4fe42901e654d6025c54d7937c13743dfc74586fc72c767c31c06.png)

Expanding, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3}-{x}_{4} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}_{3} \\ 4{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-{x}_{4} \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a basis for $\textrm{Null}(A)$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14064941/assets/60eca2d19c167355d263c471cb876e181db49ab5ac65b27561e6fb95bcc21ec0.png)

since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\textrm{Null}(A).$
